metadata.neutral_citation: CHAN PUI KI v. LEUNG ON AND ANOTHER [1996] HKCA 678; [1996] 2 HKLRD 401; [1996] 2 HKC 565; CACV 263/1995 (19 July 1996)
metadata.case_name: CHAN PUI KI v. LEUNG ON AND ANOTHER

injuries.description: She sustained severe head injuries with skull fracture. The brain injury was complicated by a left subdural haematoma which needed urgent operative decompression. There was considerable brain swelling and she was unconscious for many days.
source: She sustained severe head injuries with skull fracture. The brain injury was complicated by a left subdural haematoma which needed urgent operative decompression. There was considerable brain swelling and she was unconscious for many days.

injuries.description: She has marked spasticity of the muscles of the left upper and lower limbs. This has rendered her left hand virtually useless. The fingers tend to adopt a flexed posture, in the form of a claw.
injuries.body_part: left upper and lower limbs / left hand
source: She has marked spasticity of the muscles of the left upper and lower limbs. This has rendered her left hand virtual1y useless. The fingers tend to adopt a flexed posture, in the form of a claw.

injuries.description: Left facial paralysis, with severe cosmetic deformity.
source: She has left facial paralysis, with severe cosmetic deformity.

injuries.description: Brain damage leading to cognitive impairment (IQ found to be 86 in autumn 1993).
source: The brain damage has led to cognitive impairment. When tested in the autumn of 1993 (when the plaintiff was about 142 years old) her IQ was found to be 86: down from the 100 which Dr Leung assumed to have been her pre-accident IQ based on her average school performance.

manifestations.description: Left hand virtually useless; fingers adopt flexed 'claw' posture; writes very slowly with right hand; cannot hold the bowl with her left.
Walks with a hemiplegic gait, dragging her left leg; balance defective and tends to fall over easily.
Left facial weakness leading to involuntary dribbling of saliva from the left corner of her mouth.
Frequent right-sided headaches associated with dizzy spells lasting for as long as two days at a time; attacks can be as frequent as two to three times a week.

Psychological effects: obese, a loner, spurned by her peers; adolescent development severely prejudiced; grown mistrustful of people, feels persecuted; contemplated suicide; relationship with her mother discordant.
Activities such as cooking are effectively beyond her; very handicapped in daily living.
Virtually unemployable except in a sheltered workshop environment where average earnings about $500 per month.

treatments_received: urgent operative decompression for left subdural haematoma

losses.description: Left hand rendered virtually useless by marked spasticity; fingers adopt claw posture; left upper and lower limb spasticity.
Left facial paralysis with severe cosmetic deformity and resulting involuntary dribbling of saliva.
Walks with a hemiplegic gait, dragging her left leg; balance defective and tendency to fall.
Cognitive impairment with IQ reduced to 86.
Psychological trauma: obese, loner, spurned by peers, mistrustful, feels persecuted, contemplated suicide; adolescent development prejudiced; discordant relationship with mother.

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Unable to perform activities such as cooking; handicapped in daily living (cannot hold bowl with left hand).
Virtually unemployable except in a sheltered workshop; diminished prospects of meaningful employment and greatly diminished prospects of a happy marriage.
Prospects of a happy marriage have been greatly diminished.
